title: He was still holding the net…
paragraphs:
He was still holding the net…
when the call came.

Not clean.
Not ready.
Not worthy.
And that’s exactly when Jesus chose him.
You think God waits for your life to be fixed first.

That once you stop failing…
once you pray consistently…
once your hidden habits are gone…

Then maybe—
maybe—He will call you.

He was knee-deep in sweat, salt, and disappointment
when Jesus stepped into his boat (Luke 5:1–11).
And then Jesus says something that sounds almost offensive:
“Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch.” (Luke 5:4)
“Try again… in the place you already failed.”

Because some of you are tired not from sin—
but from trying to be faithful and seeing nothing.

You prayed.
You obeyed.
You resisted.

So now you’re smiling in public
but questioning in private.

Still showing up to church…
but your fire is flickering.

Still posting verses…
but secretly wondering if God skipped your name.
When was the last time you obeyed God after disappointment?

He could have said,
“Jesus, I’m the fisherman here. You’re the teacher.”
“Because You say so, I will let down the nets.” (Luke 5:5)
God doesn’t need your strength—He’s waiting for your surrender.
But the story doesn’t end with fish.
When Peter sees the miracle, he doesn’t celebrate.
“Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.” (Luke 5:8)

Because when holiness gets close…
sin becomes loud.
This is the part we don’t post.
The moment when success exposes your unworthiness.

The moment when God answers…
and you feel like you don’t deserve it.
Some of you are not running from sin—you’re running from being seen by a holy God.

You want the blessing…
but you’re uncomfortable with the Presence.

You want the catch…
but not the conviction.

Not denial of sin—
but invitation despite it.
“From now on you will catch men.” (Luke 5:10)

He didn’t say,
“Come back when you’re holy.”

Not behavior improvement.
Not religious performance.

Sin → exposed
Repentance → surrender
Grace → given
Redemption → lived

Every hidden compromise.
Every delayed obedience.
Every silent pride.

And on that cross,
He didn’t say, “Try harder.”
You are not called because you are worthy.
You are made worthy because you are called.
You are not “the one who failed again.”
You are the one Jesus is still calling.
You are being invited right now.

Some people stay by the boat…
admiring the miracle…
So let me speak directly to you.

The one hiding a habit.
The one delaying obedience.
The one tired of pretending you’re okay.

Not just your work—
your control.

Not just your failure—
your pride.
Because this isn’t about a post.

We’re going deeper into the moment Peter almost went back…
but grace pulled him forward again.
